translationRepairs: Book of Sui, 74th year of Volume, 39th year of Biography
卷七十四列傳第三十九 is a fascicle and biography heading, not regnal or biographical years; the replacement matches the Chinese.
Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu and rose to the post of Defender-in-Chief.
Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and rose to the post of General of the Palace Guard.

官至領軍將軍 is a palace-guard generalship, not 太尉 (Defender-in-Chief), and 章武郡王 includes Commandery; 'General Who Leads the Army' is an opaque calque, so the office is rendered as General of the Palace Guard.
Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and rose to the office of Defender-in-Chief.
Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and rose to the office of General of the Palace Guard.
The literal line likewise mistranslates 領軍將軍 as Defender-in-Chief; General of the Palace Guard is the office named in the Chinese.
When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Shiwen was further promoted to Superlative Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Viscount of Hubo, and soon appointed Governor of Beizhou.
When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Shiwen was further granted Superior Kaifu rank, enfeoffed as Viscount of Hubo, and soon appointed Governor of Beizhou.
加上開府 adds kaifu honor to the prior 開府儀同三司; 上柱國 (Superlative Pillar of State) is a different title absent from this sentence.
When Gaozu received the abdication, he was further given the rank of Superlative Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Viscount of Hubo County, and soon after appointed Governor of Beizhou.
When Gaozu received the abdication, he was further given the rank of Superior Kaifu, enfeoffed as Viscount of Hubo County, and soon after appointed Governor of Beizhou.
The literal Superlative Pillar of State is the same 上柱國 error; 加上開府 is additional Superior Kaifu.
His father's younger sister's daughter had been a concubine of Qi and was beautiful; after Qi's fall she was given to Changsun Lan, Duke of Xue, as a concubine.
His paternal cousin (daughter of his father's brother) had been a concubine of Qi and was beautiful; after Qi's fall she was given to Changsun Lan, Duke of Xue, as a concubine.
從父妹 is a female cousin through the father's brother, not a maternal uncle's or father's sister's daughter.
Under Emperor Ming of Zhou, at eighteen he was appointed Colonel and commanded local militia.
Under Emperor Ming of Zhou, at eighteen he was appointed Commander and commanded local militia.
授都督，領鄉兵 names the Northern Zhou rank 都督 commanding local militia, not the Western rank Colonel (校尉).
In the time of Emperor Ming of Zhou, at age eighteen he was appointed Colonel and commanded district troops.
In the time of Emperor Ming of Zhou, at age eighteen he was appointed Commander and commanded district troops.
The literal line repeats the same 都督/Colonel error; Commander matches the Chinese rank.
Emperor Wu heard of this with approval, promoted him to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with independent establishment, enfeoffed him as Duke of Xindu, and appointed him Governor of Yanzhou.
Emperor Wu heard of this with approval, promoted him to Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, enfeoffed him as Duke of Xindu, and appointed him Governor of Yanzhou.
進位儀同三司 is Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, not 開府儀同三司 (Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with independent establishment).
He followed the emperor in pacifying Qi and for his merit was made Superlative Pillar of State, transferred to Governor of Jianzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Liangquan.
He followed the emperor in pacifying Qi and for his merit was made Superior Kaifu, transferred to Governor of Jianzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Liangquan.
加上開府 is Superior Kaifu, not 上柱國; 'Superior Office-Opener' is an awkward calque, so the established Kaifu rendering is used.
Following the emperor in pacifying Qi, for merit he was given Superlative Pillar of State, transferred to Governor of Jianzhou, and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Liangquan County.
Following the emperor in pacifying Qi, for merit he was given Superior Kaifu, transferred to Governor of Jianzhou, and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Liangquan County.
The literal line has the same 上開府/上柱國 error; Superior Kaifu is the accurate office name.
When Gaozu assumed overall command, Wei Chong rebelled at Yecheng and Shi followed Wei Xiaokuan to attack him.
When Gaozu assumed overall command, Yuchi Jiong rebelled at Yecheng and Shi followed Wei Xiaokuan to attack him.
尉迥 is the standard abbreviation of 尉遲迥 (Yuchi Jiong); Wei Chong misreads both the Xianbei surname 尉遲 and the given name 迥.
When Gaozu assumed overall command, Wei Chong rose in rebellion at Yecheng; he followed Wei Xiaokuan to strike him.
When Gaozu assumed overall command, Yuchi Jiong rose in rebellion at Yecheng; he followed Wei Xiaokuan to strike him.
The literal field repeats the same misidentification of 尉迥 as Wei Chong.
When Gaozu accepted the throne he was made General-in-Chief of Xiangzhou and devoted himself solely to imposing his authority.
When Gaozu accepted the throne he was made Area Commander-in-Chief of Xiangzhou and devoted himself solely to imposing his authority.
拜襄州總管 is an area command (zongguan), not 大將軍 (General-in-Chief).
Upon receiving the abdication he was appointed General-in-Chief of Xiangzhou, devoting himself solely to establishing authority.
Upon receiving the abdication he was appointed Area Commander-in-Chief of Xiangzhou, devoting himself solely to establishing authority.
The literal line has the same 總管/General-in-Chief error.
His son Xin, then a court grandee, came weeping and said, "Father, you are a veteran minister of the court and have committed no grave offense.
His son Xin, then a Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, came weeping and said, "Father, you are a veteran minister of the court and have committed no grave offense.
時為儀同 abbreviates 儀同三司, a ranked honor, not a vague 'court grandee'.
His son Xin was then a Grand Master for Court Audience; he came before Shi weeping and said: "Father, you are both an old minister of the court and have committed no great fault.
His son Xin was then a Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; he came before Shi weeping and said: "Father, you are both an old minister of the court and have committed no great fault.
Grand Master for Court Audience renders 朝請大夫, not 儀同.
Soon he was appointed General-in-Chief of Guangzhou and died in office.
Soon he was appointed Area Commander-in-Chief of Guangzhou and died in office.
廣州總管 is the Guangzhou area command, not General-in-Chief.
Soon he was appointed General-in-Chief of Guangzhou and died in office.
Soon he was appointed Area Commander-in-Chief of Guangzhou and died in office.
The literal line repeats the 總管 mistranslation.
He served under the Prince of Hejian in the attack on the Turks, and for merit was made Pillar of State and transferred to General-in-Chief of Qingzhou.
He served under Hong, Prince of Hejian, in the attack on the Turks, and for merit was made Senior Pillar of State and transferred to Area Commander-in-Chief of Qingzhou.
河間王弘 names the prince 弘, which the original omits; the proposal still leaves 上柱國 as mere Pillar of State and 青州總管 as General-in-Chief.
At that time Yuan Hongsi was removed and appointed Chief Administrator of Youzhou; he feared being humiliated by Rong and firmly declined.
At that time Yuan Hongsi was appointed Chief Administrator of Youzhou; he feared being humiliated by Rong and firmly declined.
被除為幽州長史 is the appointment formula 除為, not removal from office.
For merit he was appointed Great Colonel and soon managed palace guard duty.
For merit he was appointed Grand Commander and soon managed palace guard duty.
大都督 is a high command rank, not 'Great Colonel' (a rendering of 校尉-type titles).
In the pacification of Qi he was promoted to Senior Grand Master for Court Audience and concurrently made Magistrate of Zhao Commandery.
In the pacification of Qi he was promoted to Senior Grand Master for Court Audience and concurrently made Grand Administrator of Zhao Commandery.
趙郡太守 is the commandery administrator (taishou), not a county magistrate.
When Wang Qian rebelled, Zhongqing was in Lizhou and at once joined General-in-Chief Dou Lu Ji in raising troops to resist.
When Wang Qian rebelled, Zhongqing was in Lizhou and at once joined Area Commander Dou Lu Ji in raising troops to resist.
總管豆盧勣 identifies Doulu Ji by the area-command post 總管, not 大將軍.
In the third year of Kaihuang, when the Turks raided the frontier, he served as Campaign Commander under the Prince of Hejian to Helan Mountain.
In the third year of Kaihuang, when the Turks raided the frontier, he served as Campaign Commander under Hong, Prince of Hejian, to Helan Mountain.
從河間王弘 names the prince 弘; restoring Hong does not invent or distort the Chinese.
He was transferred to Governor of Yanzhou but, before taking office, was appointed General-in-Chief of Shuozhou.
He was transferred to Governor of Yanzhou but, before taking office, was appointed Area Commander-in-chief of Shuozhou.
朔州總管 is the Shuozhou area command, not General-in-Chief.

The court feared Tardu would strike Qimin by surprise and ordered Zhongqing to station twenty thousand troops in reserve; Han Hong, Acting General-in-Chief of Daizhou, Li Yaowang, Duke of Yongkang, Liu Long, Governor of Wei, and others led ten thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Heng'an.

The court feared Tardu would strike Qimin by surprise and ordered Zhongqing to station twenty thousand troops in reserve; Han Hong, Area Commander-in-chief of Daizhou, Li Yaowang, Duke of Yongkang, Liu Long, Governor of Yuzhou, and others led ten thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Heng'an.
代州總管 is not Acting General-in-Chief; 蔚州 is Yuzhou, and 'Wei Prefecture' still collides with 魏.

The court feared Tardu would launch a surprise attack on Qimin and ordered Zhongqing to garrison twenty thousand troops in readiness; Acting General-in-Chief of Daizhou Han Hong, Duke of Yongkang Li Yaowang, and Governor of Wei Zhou Liu Long and others led ten thousand foot and horse to garrison Heng'an.

The court feared Tardu would launch a surprise attack on Qimin and ordered Zhongqing to garrison twenty thousand troops in readiness; Area Commander-in-chief of Daizhou Han Hong, Duke of Yongkang Li Yaowang, and Governor of Yuzhou Liu Long and others led ten thousand foot and horse to garrison Heng'an.
'Governor of Wei Zhou' invents a place from 蔚州, and 總管 is not Acting General-in-Chief; Yuzhou is the prefecture named.

After Emperor Wu conquered Qi he was promoted to Superlative Pillar of State and Duke of Ye, granted three thousand lengths of goods, three thousand shi of grain, a hundred slaves, and thousands of livestock.

Following Emperor Wu in destroying Qi he was promoted to Superior Kaifu and Duke of Ye County, granted three thousand lengths of goods, three thousand shi of grain, a hundred slaves, and thousands of livestock.
從武帝滅齊 marks accompaniment; 上開府 is not 上柱國, and 鄴縣公 is Duke of Ye County; 'Superlative Opening Office' is an awkward calque.
Xin sent Hongdu to admonish him with warnings of fortune and ruin; Chen withdrew by evening.
Xin sent Hongdu to admonish him with warnings of fortune and ruin; Pan Chen withdrew by evening.
琛 is Pan Chen's given name from the preceding sentence (陳將潘琛); bare 'Chen' collapses the person into the Chen polity.
When Wei Chong rebelled, Hongdu served as Campaign Commander under Wei Xiaokuan.
When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Hongdu served as Campaign Commander under Wei Xiaokuan.
尉迥 is Yuchi Jiong; 'Wei Jiong' still misreads 尉遲 as Wei and collides with 韋孝寬 in the same sentence.
He was soon transferred to General-in-Chief of Xiangzhou.
He was soon transferred to Area Commander-in-Chief of Xiangzhou.
襄州總管 is the Xiangzhou area command, not General-in-Chief.
When the Liang prince Xiao Cong came to court, the emperor appointed Hongdu General-in-Chief of Jiangling to garrison Jingzhou.
When the Liang prince Xiao Cong came to court, the emperor appointed Hongdu Area Commander-in-Chief of Jiangling to garrison Jingzhou.
江陵總管 is the Jiangling area command, not General-in-Chief.
When Wei Chong rebelled at Xiangzhou, he joined his elder brother Hongdu in attacking him and for merit was appointed Senior Grand Master for Court Audience.
When Yuchi Jiong rebelled at Xiangzhou, he joined his elder brother Hongdu in attacking him and for merit was appointed Senior Grand Master for Court Audience.
尉迥作亂相州 is Yuchi Jiong's rebellion at Xiangzhou, not a person named Wei Chong.
When Wei Chong rebelled at Xiangzhou, he joined his elder brother Hongdu in attacking him and for merit was appointed Senior Grand Master for Court Audience.
When Yuchi Jiong rebelled at Xiangzhou, he joined his elder brother Hongdu in attacking him and for merit was appointed Senior Grand Master for Court Audience.
The literal field repeats the same 尉迥/Wei Chong misidentification.
Soon he was further given the rank of Superlative Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Marquis of Huangtai County with a fief of eight hundred households.
Soon he was further given the rank of Superior Kaifu, enfeoffed as Marquis of Huangtai County with a fief of eight hundred households.
加上開府 is Superior Kaifu, not 上柱國; 'Senior Commander Unequaled in Honor' conflates 上開府 with 儀同三司.
Soon he was further given the rank of Superlative Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Marquis of Huangtai County with a fief of eight hundred households.
Soon he was further given the rank of Superior Kaifu, enfeoffed as Marquis of Huangtai County with a fief of eight hundred households.
The literal line has the same 上開府 error; Senior Commander Unequaled in Honor is not that office.

Yet Hongdu managed his household like an office; his sons and younger brothers, though gray-haired, were beaten and flogged when they moved; the inner gates were stern and orderly, and he was praised by his contemporaries.

Yet Hongdu managed his household like an office; his sons and younger brothers, though gray-haired, were beaten and flogged at the slightest move; the inner gates were stern and orderly, and he was praised by his contemporaries.
動行捶楚 means they were flogged for any action, not that they were beaten when they moved house.
Later, because of his status as an imperial relative, his treatment grew still more generous and he was made General-in-Chief of Xiang Prefecture.
Later, because of his status as an imperial relative, his treatment grew still more generous and he was made Area Commander-in-Chief of Xiang Prefecture.
遷襄州總管 is an area command, not General-in-Chief.
During Kaihuang he was appointed Grand Master for Court Audience for military merit, then Assistant Administrator of Guizhou.
During Kaihuang he was appointed Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers for military merit, then Assistant Administrator of Guizhou.
儀同 is 儀同三司, not 朝請大夫; 'Equal-in-Rites (Yitong)' is awkward beside the established rendering used elsewhere in this chapter.
In Kaihuang for military merit he was appointed Grand Master for Court Audience; soon he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Guizhou.
In Kaihuang for military merit he was appointed Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; soon he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Guizhou.
The literal Grand Master for Court Audience is the same 儀同 error; the parenthetical Yitong calque is still unnatural.
When Emperor Yang succeeded he was summoned as Vice Director of the Imperial Household; for offending the throne he was sent out as Assistant Governor of Hengshan.
When Emperor Yang succeeded he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; for offending the throne he was sent out as Assistant Governor of Hengshan.
光祿少卿 is vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments (光祿寺), not the Imperial Household (a Han 光祿勳 sense).
